data.title: Maximum Entertainment Moves to Half-Year Reporting and Will Not Publish an Interim Report for the Third Quarter of 2026
data.description:
Stockholm, Sweden (November 6, 2026) - Maximum Entertainment AB (Nasdaq: MAXENT B) ("Maximum Entertainment" or the "Company") today announces that it is moving from quarterly to half-year financial reporting. As a consequence, the interim report for the third quarter of 2026, previously scheduled for publication on November 30, 2026, will not be published. The Company's next financial report will be the year-end report for the financial year 2026, which will be published on March 31, 2027.

The decision has been made following the Company's U.S. subsidiary, Maximum Entertainment, LLC, agreeing to stipulate to the appointment of a court-supervised receiver, and after deliberations with the Company’s auditors.

For more information about Maximum Entertainment, please visit: www.maximument.com.

data.title: Kunal Kamra takes a dig at Deepinder Goyal over Temple wearable, questions scientific claims
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 6 -- Comedian Kunal Kamra has taken a swipe at entrepreneur Deepinder Goyal over his defence of Temple, an experimental wearable that Goyal claims can measure blood flow in the brain in real time. The exchange comes after Goyal addressed concerns raised by doctors about the device's scientific claims and the evidence supporting its technology.

Kamra in a post on X mocked Goyal's defence of Temple, arguing that it relied heavily on his personal investment, wealth and confidence in the device rather than addressing the scientific and medical concerns raised by doctors. He also questioned the promise of future validation, the involvement of employees and the company's claims of groundbreaking features, suggesting that the entrepreneur was asking critics to wait years for proof.

Kamra was responding to a post by Goyal, who addressed what he described as concerns among Indian doctors about Temple. In his post, Goyal defended the device's business model, investment and approach to scientific validation.

Goyal said the company had already spent $30 million building Temple, of which $20 million was his own money. He argued that selling a few thousand devices would recover only a small fraction of that investment.

He also cited the company's return policy, writing: "First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple. We have 14-day, no-questions-asked returns (which even Apple doesn't offer in India). If the product doesn't work, it fails out of the gate and the company dies before recovering a tenth of its R&D."

Goyal said he had left the Eternal CEO role to pursue what he described as a purpose-driven project with Temple. He added that his financial position meant he was not pursuing the venture for quick monetary gains.

"I left the Eternal CEO role to chase purpose with Temple. This is not about money. I have enough of it to last for generations. My incentives are fully aligned with getting the science right. I am not staking a reputation earned over 20 years on making a quick buck," he wrote.

Addressing questions about the evidence behind the wearable, Goyal said pre-prints were expected before peer-reviewed publications. He also referred to the development timelines of other wearable technology companies.

"Most wearable companies start with internal studies. Whoop shipped its band in 2015, and the first published validation followed a few years later. We hold ourselves to a higher standard; pre-prints are a step prior to peer reviewed publications, and they are coming up," Goyal wrote.

He added that the company believed the product had reached a stage where it was valuable enough for people to pay for and use, while further validation continued.

"At some point you have to stick your neck out and say: we believe in our science, and the product is now valuable enough for people to pay for and use. We believe we are there. More validation continues in public," he said.

Goyal also said the company's claims could be verified by individuals and institutions and that independent studies would emerge once the device became available for use.

He added that some of Temple's features had not yet been made public.

Dubbed Temple, the device is a metallic-coloured, clip-like wearable that Goyal claims can measure cerebral blood flow (CBF) in real time.

According to Goyal, the experimental health-tech device can measure cerebral blood flow in a manner similar to a "miniaturised" MRI.

Cerebral blood flow refers to the circulation of blood through the brain, which supplies it with the oxygen and nutrients required to function. It is said to usually remain unchanged or decline only minimally during ageing.

Temple is currently not a Zomato product and is not available for public or commercial use. Goyal has, however, indicated that the device is "getting there".

The debate around Temple centres on the scientific evidence supporting its claims and the extent of validation available before the product reaches consumers. Goyal has said further validation is under way, while Kamra's response has brought renewed attention to the questions being raised about the device.

data.title: US oil and gas rig count rises to highest level since 2024, Baker Hughes says
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino

US energy firms this week added rigs for the first time in four weeks, pushing the number to the highest since May 2024, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by one to 604 in the week to November 6. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 56, or 10%, from this time last year.

It also said the number of oil rigs rose by one to 463 this week, the highest level since May 2025, while the gas rig count rose by one to 131, its highest since mid-October. The number of miscellaneous rigs fell by one to 10, the lowest since early October, Baker Hughes said.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

With spot US West Texas Intermediate crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years, due to supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran, the US Energy Information Administration now projects that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, the EIA projects output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day in 2025 to 112.2 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises from power plants serving data centers and from liquefied natural gas exports.

data.title: US Senator Murphy to miss Senate votes for weeks as he recovers from stroke
data.description:
Democratic US Senator Chris Murphy said on Friday he would miss the next several weeks of votes in the Senate as he continues his recovery from a stroke.

"In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today," the Connecticut senator said in a statement.

Murphy suffered a small hemorrhagic stroke on October 31, said Jose Suarez, chief of Neurosciences Critical Care at the Johns Hopkins Hospital.

"He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation," Suarez said in the statement.

data.title: Soybeans rise off 12-week low on short-covering
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures edged higher on Friday, supported by short covering and bargain buying, after sliding earlier to a 12-week low.

An influx of freshly harvested soybeans and corn from US farmers' fields has weighed on prices.

Traders adjusted positions ahead of the US Department of Agriculture issuing updated crop forecasts next week. Analysts, on average, expect the agency to increase its estimate of US soybean production to a record-large 4.597 billion bushels from 4.562 billion in October, according to a Reuters poll.

Large crop forecasts have helped fuel long liquidation by commodity funds, traders said.

"The biggest problem you have in the market right now is you still have too many longs in the soybean complex," said Jim Gerlach, president of A/C Trading.

Most-active soybean futures traded as low as $11.84 per bushel, the lowest level since August 14, before rising 3-1/4 cents to $11.91-1/2 in afternoon trading.

CBOT corn traded as low as $4.38-1/2 a bushel, the lowest since July 1, a level corn also touched on Wednesday. Futures then rebounded and were last up 2 cents at $4.42 a bushel.

Analysts, on average, expect the USDA to peg US corn production at 15.962 billion bushels next week, down from its October estimate of 16.034 billion. The harvest would be the second largest in history, after last year's crop.

"Rains have finally moved out of the heart of the country and a strong corn harvest is set to resume across the belt next week," consultancy StoneX said.

CBOT wheat slid on prospects of a resumption of Black Sea grain exports after Russia and Ukraine confirmed participation in three-way peace talks with the US in Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11.

Wheat futures were down 5-3/4 cents at $5.93-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: White House recasts Trump arch as military tribute
data.description:
Key points:
  • New website names project Military Triumphal Arch near Arlington National Cemetery entrance
  • Federal Aviation Administration greenlit project in September despite aviation safety concerns
  • Interior Department documents say construction is expected to take two to three years

By Bo Erickson

Hours after a US judge paused construction on President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot (76.2-meter) arch in Washington, the White House on Friday shared new depictions portraying the project as a tribute to the nation's military heritage, the latest attempt to rebrand it amid mounting opposition.

The site unveiled on Friday calls the project, which would stand near the entrance of Arlington National Cemetery, the Military Triumphal Arch.

Animated images show a trio of gilded, winged statues above the words “GOLDEN AGE OF AMERICA,” written in gold letters set against stone. A flame emanates from a torch in the hands of one of the winged female figures.

The White House shared the new renderings from a group called the United States Triumphal Arch Foundation. Its listed chairman, former Trump-appointed ambassador Randy Evans, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump has increasingly turned his attention to a series of major projects in Washington, both before and after his Republican Party suffered massive losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections that cost the party control of Congress.

The arch and Trump’s other signature projects have drawn significant political and legal opposition.

The attorneys general from Virginia and the District of Columbia have sued to prevent construction of the arch, which they say will irreparably damage the skyline of the nation's capital and surrounding area, including Arlington National Cemetery, the nation's most revered resting ground for service men and women, and the nearby Lincoln Memorial.

Some aviation ​experts also raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport. However, the Federal Aviation Administration greenlit the project in September.

The president previously justified the arch as a "military complex" to be used for drones and snipers. The new renderings indicate the arch is also now dedicated to the nation's military history.

The National Capital Planning Commission, a regional authority, voted on Thursday to approve the arch project after hearing from about 100 opponents, including Democratic lawmakers. Hours later, US District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a 14-day restraining order on construction, saying it would last about three years and "disrupt traffic, ​create noise, result in large-scale excavation, and more."

The Trump administration contends Congress approved the arch more than 100 ​years ago when it also authorized construction of a bridge across the Potomac River.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle on Friday said the federal ruling came from "an activist district court" and added, "We are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds and look forward to seeing the completion of this magnificent Arch — a tribute to 250 years of American greatness.”

Construction is expected to take two to three years, according to Interior Department documents submitted to the planning commission on Thursday.

data.title: Iren Shares Climb as AI Compute Demand, Pricing Power Boosts 1Q Revenue
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of Iren rose after the neocloud narrowed its loss and reported higher revenue in the fiscal first quarter, driven by strong demand for artificial-intelligence cloud capacity that has increased pricing power.

Shares climbed 19% at $21.42 in Friday afternoon trading. The stock has fallen from its May peak as investors increasingly scrutinize the financial sustainability of the AI infrastructure buildout. Shares have fallen 43% year-to-date.

The company on Thursday reported a fiscal first-quarter loss of $263 million, compared with a loss of $684 million in the previous fourth quarter. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting a loss of $254.4 million.

Revenue rose 66% from the previous quarter to $228 million, beating analyst expectations for $217.9 million.

Of that total, AI cloud services revenue contributed $135 million, while AI cloud lease revenue rose to $65 million.

The company said its pricing power continues to grow. Iren estimated that contracted pricing on three-year deals rose 11% since the previous quarter, with pricing for five-year deals up 12%.

"We own the land, the power and the data centers under all of it, which gives us more ways to fund growth and lets us set its pace," co-Chief Executive Officer Daniel Roberts said.

Iren had been targeting more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue by the end of the year. The company said Thursday that the target is fully contracted and funded, but that supplier timing and a change requested by a customer have pushed back the target to January, with the possibility of a further extension to February.

The company ended the quarter with a revenue backlog of $20.3 billion, up 22% quarter-over-quarter.
